whether it be professional, spiritual, personal relationships,

you'll start defining, you know, I know what I don't want,

The next part is to overcome the obstacles of figuring out specifically what you do want.
And I'm going to give you three kinds of obstacles that show up, three that I've seen most often.
The first one is selfishness.
We are literally taught that having what we want, going for what we want, thinking about ourselves is selfish.
Particularly if we grew up in brothers and sisters.
Going and trying to satisfy our own desires usually was at somebody else's expense or somebody else not being able to do what they wanted to do.
Then one of the stories we got from mom and dad or in school was learn to play fair, let your brother have, sister have a turn.
And that went along with the story, don't be selfish.
And so we learn to associate having and going for what we want with being selfish.
And of course, nobody wants to be selfish.
Nobody wants to be perceived as selfish.
You know, that's not very kind and loving and spiritual,
and nobody wants to be with a quote-unquote selfish person who just thinks of themselves.
You know, so there's a lot of agreements we have about that word, about that term,
that inhibit us from really saying, you know, this is what I want for me.
What we have to do is reframe that word.
And so I'll invite you to go back to a core belief inventory on specifically that word, selfish.
being selfish? Where are the places you think or believe that you're selfish? And what does that

What we need to do is reframe what is selfish versus what is taking care of ourselves.
What is really serving ourselves and honoring ourselves?
Because if you are serving and honoring yourself,

You can do it without being unkind to other people.
One of the voices in your mind may tell you otherwise.

So I think we can forge ahead and tackle that resistance at this point.
I'll give you an example of this.

But I know a mom who's got adult children in their 20s, hung up on addictions, and she's still writing checks for their utility bills so they can keep the lights on.

But the logic she has in her mind is,
no, if I just keep this money for myself and do what I want to do,

That story of selfish is self-abusive.
So she's giving her money to her daughter, who's abusing herself with it through drugs,
and at the same time abusing herself, not allowing herself to have her own life,
because allowing herself to have her own life would be selfish.
That is the power of that word, that kind of belief that we have to scrutinize.
She knows giving money to her addicted daughter isn't helping,
but one of the reasons she can't stop is, she says, if I don't give it, I'm being selfish.
So when she frees herself up from that agreement, now she cannot give and both serve herself and
serve her daughter. And that is being generous. So the big paradigm shift is when you give to
yourself and you allow yourself to have what you want, that isn't necessarily being selfish in my
point of view. That is learning to be generous. It's learning to be generous with yourself.
and if you're more generous with yourself, you will have more.
And if you have more love, more abundance,
more of what you want in your life, more happiness,
you will have more that you can give to other people
in terms of time and attention and love.
Until you really give to yourself,
you won't have very much that you can give to another.
So practicing generosity with yourself
is a big step in being able to be generous with other people.
So that's a resistance and a paradigm shift in an interpretation about selfishness to generosity that a lot of people find they need to make.
May or may not apply to you.
Second obstacle is when we were kids, typically growing up, when there was something we wanted,

okay, we want such and such for Christmas or our birthday,

At other times, if we did something they didn't want us to do,

They took away our dessert.
then even wanting something can trigger in our mind, oh, it might be taken away.

And I will be unhappy if I don't get what I want.
Therefore, one of the mechanisms we started to create in order to avoid disappointment, painful loss,

People who, after a heartbreak, are convinced love hurts,

oh, I had the relationship, my desires were fulfilled,

We start defining things in terms of,

has to do with our life.

Your Training

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-your-training-6431667



Summary of practice

1. Listen to the What You Want lesson audio

2. Write out what you DON’T want. Then begin writing about what you want
in your day and life.

3. Break it out to separate areas of your life. Emotional, Financial, home,
relationships, work, spiritual, and most importantly, emotionally.



Some notes

Sometimes get into the details of what you want. I was doing this exercise with a client.
He had made out his list of what he wanted in relationship. It was the typical list of what
he would want in a partner that you would find on Match.com.

I asked him how he wanted to resolve conflicts. He was a bit stunned and sat quietly. It
dawned on him that this was an important component of relationships, but that he had
written out his fantasy relationship. In the fantasy there were no problems. It was a fairy
tale.

The term “conflict” can have a huge range of meaning. Men and women often have a
different definition of this word. To a man it often means arguments and fights. To a
woman it is just resolving differences that get talked about like what time to leave a party
or where to go to dinner. How do you share the trade offs of choices and how do each of
you feel when that happens? Even in good relationships you won’t always agree. But the
experience of not agreeing has a spectrum of possibilities.

Do you want to be listened to, heard, and respected?

There might be emotional reactions from old belief systems, or past relationship patterns
that get projected on your current partner. How do you want your partner to respond
when you do it? How are you going to own the projecting that you do, and how do you
want to talk about it. (PS The Recapitulation series is very good at addressing past
memories, emotions, and behaviors and releasing them.)

How do you want your partner to respond? What kind of conversation do you want to
have with them. In your ideal world of consciously working through issues, how on your
best day, do you envision dealing with your old emotional patterns that you are still




                                                                                                               1/2

working on? How do you want to resolve these projections if your partner does them?

This is a bit deeper and realistic. It also bypasses the Princess version of “what you want”
which is probably going to have too much fantasy. Yes, ask for the fantasy, and know that
you may have to work through some old history to create it.

If you want a certain financial income, you also need to balance it with reality. What are
you making right now, and what is a realistic increase? If your financial goals require that
you win the lottery, then I suggest you rewrite your list with a plan B and practical
solution path as well.

It’s not enough to just write out what you want. You have to make a plan of actions, take
action, and get motivated. We will work on this in the next lessons. Just getting in touch
with what you want, feeling desire, and identifying some of the possible resistance
elements is enough for this step.





                                                                                                               2/2

title: Module 23-What You Want-23- SM - What You Want - 02 Obstacles you are likely to find
method: Text extracted from the original written course handout.

pages.text:
Obstacles you are likely to find

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-obstacles-you-are-likely-to-find-6431669

Sometimes when I give this assignment to clients they start to imagine how happy they
can be, and how good their life can be. Immediately, or shortly thereafter, this brings up
feelings of unworthiness, shame, and fear.

By just imagining being happy and the desire for it, they find the edges of their comfort
zone or what you might call limiting beliefs, or the walls of their emotional safety. There
arises the countering beliefs to feeling good and happy. Some of these might be, “I don’t
deserve those things. I don’t deserve to be happy. I’m afraid that if I have them that they
will be taken away. etc.”

At first this might be an “oh crap” moment. Some characters might use those opposing
emotions to feel defeated. However, if you step out of those stories, perhaps you can look
at the upside. The upside is that you have found beliefs of a false sense of identity that has
been unconsciously opposing your happiness.

Now that you have found it, you can work on exposing it further, releasing the emotions
and beliefs out of your unconscious. That means writing about the characters and
emotions that show up. By removing these obstacle beliefs you have been tripping over
you can move more effectively to the life you want. Running into parts of your belief
system that are afraid of getting what you want, or even feeling the desire for it is a big
success.

Selfishness

When we were children, and particularly with siblings, we were shamed for wanting
things. "Who do you think you are?" "You have to share with your sister, don't be
selfish." Shame and the label of selfishness became connected to the desire for what you
want. Don't be surprised if these feelings and labels show up in this process. If they do,
then you are on the right path to getting in touch with your hearts desire.

Some other narratives might be related to pleasing others. Here you are countering the
Prostitute/Pleaser programming. It is covering up the victim emotions of unworthiness
and shame. “I don’t deserve to be happy on my own, or have these good feelings. The
only way to get acceptance is to please others so much that they like me and give me
approval, acceptance, and love.” This is the conditioning that love is conditional. At
some point you decide that love for your self is a good thing.

 Avoiding Disappointment

Second resistant point is not allowing yourself to feel desire. “I will be unhappy if I don’t
get what I want…” so to avoid that pain of missing out or losing it later I will suppress the
feeling of desire. Don't try and you won't get disappointed or frustrated because you never




                                                                                                               1/2

expected it in the first place.

The mind has much stronger beliefs about avoiding pain than it does for creating love,
joy, and happiness. Don’t be surprised when these show up. Okay, be surprised for a little
bit, and then inventory them as stories from your characters.

 I have to get it Perfect

Feeling like you need to get it perfect, and the pressure of getting it “right” pushes our
attention away from feeling that desire. Under that pressure, we freeze for fear of
designing our “whole life” wrong. To counter this “big pressure” of getting our "whole
life" right, break it down into steps. After all, you don’t try to eat the meal in one bite.
Same with creating your life.

It is an iterative process anyways. When you left high school you could only see the next
step. When I left high school I went to study engineering. At the time there was no
internet and so businesses involving the internet weren’t on my radar. I could only choose
from what I saw.

Later in life, the world changes, and now much of my business runs using internet
technology. I couldn’t have seen the possibilities for my life the way it is now when I was
in high school. Not only did I not have the imagination developed, but the technology in
the world didn’t exist.

Nor was I developed enough to have something to offer.

Even today, I am revamping what I want. I am creating a new list of what I want based on
who I am now. I am currently doing the next iteration of my life. I have outgrown, or am
outgrowing the previous version of myself. What I want five years from now will be
different from what I want now and so I will redo this exercise.

You have permission to do the same. You can change your self, and your goals later. For
now, make the next version you can for yourself. Once you move down that road you may
have a better vision of what is possible. From that new vision you can create a new list of
what you want.





                                                                                                               2/2

title: Module 23-What You Want-23- SM - What You Want - 03 Common Questions
method: Text extracted from the original written course handout.

pages.text:
Common Questions

   selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-common-questions-6431670

How do I get more in touch with what I desire?

Allowing yourself to feel desire often goes against earlier belief programming. I
recommend noticing when you feel some desire for something, and to honor it. That
means go do the thing you want however small. You are training your mind that it is okay
to have that feeling of desire and to signal your conscious mind It will be allowed and
honored.

If you notice that you have an impulse for ice cream, then follow that desire and act on it.
You are noticing the feeling of desire, and you are connecting that feeling to action. You
are allowing yourself to complete the circuit of having a desire, and informing your
mind/belief system to act on it and have what you want. In this way you are no longer
suppressing the feeling of desire. This is what I mean by honoring it.

When you have the impulse of desire, and you don’t act on it, you are suppressing that
feeling. Your nervous system/belief system learns to override and suppress those feelings
of what you want.

In those cases when you choose not to act on it (I want ice cream but it is 10:30pm), then
at least have some gratitude for the feeling of desire. This is rewarding your nervous
system for sending you a desire signal. You are giving your self the positive reinforcement
of gratitude.

If you have the feeling that, you want to go for a walk, hike, nap, swim, meditation retreat,
etc. Whatever the desire, is, notice it, and when you can act on it, do so.

Also notice what you do to suppress those feelings of desire and how you talk your way
out of not doing it. What characters are those? How do they repress the good feelings and
what are they replaced with. Does it sound like, “no, I really should get back to working on
that project.” This is a saboteur of happiness. Look out for how this belief program is
suppressing your desire. It might also be very productive, but how much does this
“productive character” allow you to have feelings and enjoy your life?



What if I don't know what I want?

Start small. Start writing what you want for today. Write out what you want for the week.

Notice that your judge, perfectionist, or hero might want to write your list. Maybe that’s
the best list you know how to write. Then go after what is on that list, and enjoy it. That
will help you desire more and have more enjoyment.





                                                                                                               1/2

Write out what you want for dinner. What do you want it to taste like? What do you want
the smile on your face to feel like? Maybe you don’t know what you want because the
question is overwhelming. There are too many things to want. So, make the question
smaller to begin with.





                                                                                                               2/2

Lesson Transcript

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-lesson-transcript-6588435

Hi, this is Gary van Warmerdam with the self-mastery audio course and this session is
about creating what you want. A lot of this program is about creating what you want but
this is just one step in the process. This step is about defining what you want and if you’ve
been going along at this point you might’ve found that that’s changed or you don’t know
what you want anymore because a lot of what we wanted was driven by an image of
perfection of the mind, something in our belief system that says this is what I should be,
this is what I should have, this is what my life should look like and you find out that those
were a lot of expectations, were dreams that other people put in your mind and it wasn’t
really what you wanted.

And so as you go through and you dismantle those beliefs, that isn’t really what I want,
that isn’t what makes me happy. That’s what society has kind of presented. This is what
I’m supposed to want. Well as you dissolve that, which the tools in the first session to be
allowing you to do and you may not be completely done yet but doesn’t need to be
completely done before you start the next process of re-creating a new dream of what you
want but as that dissolves you might be left feeling like you’re in no man’s land. I don’t
know what I want and you might also find that you want a lot of things and that can be
kind of paralyzing because you’ve got so many directions to go you can’t accomplish them
all, found a new level of inspiration for so many things.

And so now you don’t have time to do it all. Most commonly what we find, what I found
with people is they don’t know what they want. It’s like they try to think about it but
nothing comes to mind. So we are going to go at this process and is going to include those
other people who have, want too many things and can’t figure out which direction to go
but we also want to specifically address those things that we don’t know what we want.
We are not sure which first of all is a completely okay place to be. Just being aware, that’s
where you are, big bonus. You can figure it out from there. I am going to give you steps to
do that. We are going to go at this a little sideways because you will find out I do things
more sideways.

The first step in the process of figuring out what you want is to first figure out and buy
figure out I mean right down on a piece of paper so it’s very clear in your journal where
ever you are tracking all this, so it’s very clear to you because it forces you to clarify
instead of leaving it in ambiguous terms in your mind. That very process of running it
down help you define it. So the first step is to write down, clarify what you don’t want,
what is it that you don’t want and by creating this list it may spark some ideas later of
what you do want because you may look for the opposite and specifically for me there are
things that I don’t want in relationships, people who are unkind, disrespectful, angry.

I can make a very detailed list of what I don’t want and that includes both personal and
professional. It doesn’t mean there aren’t people who are angry with me. I just, I am not
going to spend a lot of time having lunch with them or anytime at all having lunch with



                                                                                                               1/9

them because this is something I clearly don’t want, then define that list, be specific, look
at experiences in your life that were unpleasant and look for the kind of specific things
that you don’t want whether be professional, spiritual, personal relationships,
professional relationships, financial.

Breakout any of those areas in your life or in further however you want to do it and what
you’d specifically don’t want in each area and pay particular attention to the emotional
qualities, the emotional aspects that you don’t want. We will talk about why that is later.
And once you have this list it may start to help spur some ideas of what you do want, they
start defining I know I don’t want and these are the kind of relationships or experiences or
types of things that I want to be doing. If you don’t want to be to bored that’s what you
don’t want, then what you do want is to be in action. It doesn’t mean you have to create
emotional drama but being in action, doing things outdoors, socializing with friends.
These are things that you do want.

What kind of friends, what is the emotional quality, what’s the interaction, is it funny, is it
intellectual, how is it engaging to you that it’s enjoyable? This is something that can spark
this process. The next part is to overcome the obstacles of figuring out specifically what
you do want and I am going to give you three kinds of obstacles that show up, three that
I’ve seen most often.

The first one is selfishness. We are literally taught that having what we want, going for
what we want, thinking about ourselves is selfish. Particularly if we grew up with brothers
and sisters. Going and trying to satisfy our own desires usually was it somebody else’s
expense or somebody else not been able to do what they wanted to do. Then one of the
stories we got from mom and dad or in school was learn to play fair, let your brother have,
sister have a turn and that went along with the story don’t be selfish and so we learn to
associate, having and going for what we want with being selfish and of course nobody
wants to be selfish. Nobody wants to be perceived as selfish, now that’s not very kind and
loving and spiritual and nobody was to be with a “selfish person” who just thinks of
themselves and so there’s a lot of agreements we have about that word, about that term
that inhibit us from really saying you know this is what I want for me.

What we have to do is reframe that word and so I will invite you to go back to a core belief
inventory on specifically that word selfish, being selfish. Where are the places you think or
believe that you’re selfish and what is that keep you from doing? Where do you play the
prostitute role in that regard? And not ask for what you want, respect your own desires
and act out in this kind of behavior. What we need to do is reframe what is selfish versus
what is taking care of ourselves. What is really serving ourselves and honoring ourselves
because if you are serving and honoring yourself you can do it without being selfish, you
can do without being unkind to other people.

One of the voices in your mind may tell you otherwise but you know we probably learned
by now that it’s those voices in our mind, they are liars so I think we can forge ahead and
tackle that resistance at this point. I will give you an example and this is a classic case with
most often the biggest culprit is a mother of children. More than one mother I know has
sacrificed themselves, disrespected themselves to the degree of giving away their time,



                                                                                                               2/9

their energy, their money to their children who may or may not appreciate it without
really taking care of themselves and that’s understandable when your kids are small but I
know a mom who’s got adult children in their 20s, hung up on addictions and she is still
writing checks for their utility bills so they can get the lights on and that money prevents
her from having the life she wants when she knows darn well that what her daughter is
going to go do with that money is spend it on alcohol and drugs but the logic she has in
her mind is, no if I just keep this money for myself and do what I want to do, have a nice
dinner out with friends or go to a restaurant and have a nice evening, if I spend the money
for that the voice in her mind tells her she’s being selfish so this story of selfish can run to
that degree.

That story of selfish is self-abusive so she’s giving her money to her daughter who is
abusing herself with it through drugs and at the same time abusing herself, not allowing
herself to have her own life because allowing yourself to have her own life would be
selfish. That is the power, that word, that kind of belief that we have to scrutinize. She
knows giving money to her addicted daughter isn’t helping but one of the reason she can’t
stop is, says if I don’t give it I’m being selfish. So when she frees herself up from that
agreement, now she cannot give and both serve herself answer for daughter and that is
being generous.

So the big paradigm shift is when you give to yourself and you allow yourself to have what
you want that isn’t necessarily being selfish in my point of view. That is learning to be
generous. It’s learning to be generous with yourself and if you’re more generous with
yourself you will have more and if you have more love, more abundance, more of what you
want in your life, more happiness you will have more that you can give to other people in
terms of time and attention and love.

Until you really give to yourself you won’t have very much that you can give to another, so
practicing generosity with yourself is a big step in being able to be generous with other
people. so that’s a resistance on a paradigm shift and an interpretation about selfishness
to generosity that a lot of people find they need to make. It may or may not apply to you.

Second obstacle is when we were kids typically growing up when there was something we
wanted it could very often have been that that thing that we wanted was used as a
punishment against us. Very simply if we wanted a dessert we had to eat all the vegetables
on our plate before we could have the reward called dessert that we wanted. Then there
was at times a price to pay for what we wanted and it was a way if our parents knew what
we wanted okay we want such and such for Christmas or our birthday okay then we have
to go do ABCD and E or maybe it’s just A in order to get that. To go play with friends we
had to clean up our room.

So parents use this kind of information about what we wanted to get us to do things, to
control us. At other times if we did something they didn’t want us to do, broke one of the
rules in the house or broke a vase they would take away what we wanted, they took away
our weekend or visit to friends, they took away our dessert. Then even wanting something





                                                                                                               3/9

can trigger on our mind oh it might be taken away. If it’s taken away we will have an
emotional reaction, which is we will create emotional reaction. We didn’t know we were
creating it back then and I will be unhappy if I don’t get what I want.

Therefore one of the mechanisms we started to create in order to avoid disappointment,
painful loss was not to want. You can see this in relationships. People who after a
heartbreaker convinced love hurts, it’s not worth it, I don’t want to get involved with
anybody and they’re very tentative about getting involved in a relationship. What happens
is in their mind they associate that pain of loss in the relationship and disappointment
and heartbreak with satisfying the desire of what they want. Oh I had a relationship, my
desires were fulfiled but when it went away it was so painful. It’s not worth to have it. Well
if you see that having the relationship with someone you love is a completely separate
emotional dynamic thing, the emotion of pain that we create in a heartbreak then you say
you know what I can do the relationship without doing the pain even if the relationship
doesn’t last.

And you start to see oh that’s a separate dynamic, a separate set of agreements in my
mind and there are separate things we do with our mind and our beliefs and our stories
and separate characters that are driven and when we can clarify that which is I can go
have what I want and if it doesn’t happen, if it goes away I don’t have to make a big
reaction about it. So the second part of not having what we want is maybe in those stories
in our history and our core belief is we associate some kind of pain with fulfilling the
desire of what we want so that may be something to put in the inventory process as an
obstacle and resistance to dissolve so that you can really start to see what is it that I want
because as long as we associate a lot of pain with that desire we are going to have a hard
time seeing it because we don’t want the pain that our core belief system associate with
what we want.

The third obstacle I see to figuring out what we want is the one where we get
overwhelmed. We start defining things in terms of what we start creating in our mind
what we want has to do with our life. Of course it has to do with our life, it has to do with
our relationships, our careers, where we want to be and how we want to live for the next
20 years and when we look at that, next 20, 30, 40 years we can become overwhelmed, is
too much, you can’t know ,you can’t know where all this is going but our mind tries to
define things and picture it out that far and the other part of picturing it out that far is
now there’s a huge amount of pressure to get it right because if we get it wrong and we are
going in the wrong direction the consequences of living a life we don’t want for the next
30 years is so high.

I better not get it wrong and so there’s a tentativeness to define the journey, to define the
destination of what we really want in those terms because by God we had better get it
right because it’s a very big deal. Well here’s a newsflash you don’t have to get it right, you
don’t have to figure it all out now, you don’t have to know what you want and even if you
figured out and find this is what I want for my life, understand you have total permission
to change it and this is what I encourage you actually to do to set it up so you have
permission to change when you want in defining your life to make it small enough so it’s a




                                                                                                               4/9

doable project because 20, 40, 60, 80 years is a big project and we can pretty much know
for a fact that five years from now or 10 years from now we will know things about
ourselves and will be a different person that what we want has changed entirely.

So let’s count for that, let’s count on the fact that five years from now or 10 years from
now or even just one year from now we are going to be a different person than we are
now. We’re going to have to learn things, grown be looking at things differently and
perhaps what we want has changed entirely or maybe just a little bit, who knows but let’s
put that in the plan and that’s why instead of figuring out what you want for your life, I
want you to figure out what you want for the next year or six months or two years
whatever that interim timeframe is then you say okay these are the things I want, maybe
it’s a different business, it’s a different job or I want to get a Masters degree and you know
it’s going to take a certain amount of time.

Then you say this is what I want and this is what I am going to commit to now and in six
months, a year, two years, whatever it is I am going to reevaluate and create a new life
based on what I know two years from now. I don’t know what I will know in two years
from now but I know it will be different than what I know now and that person living in
that consciousness is going to design the new life whoever I grow it to.

So don’t make a big deal out of it, don’t put a lot of pressure on yourself to get it right
because you don’t have to get it right for your life, what you’re going to do is you are going
to create what I call a practice life, one that you’re going to go work on for a year or
whatever the timeframe is, develop it and one of the big things about creating a practice
life is you are going to be practicing and creating. You are going to learn how to attract
things into your life you’re going to learn how to operate differently being a new person.
Integrate all these skills that you are learning or techniques whether it’s in this program
or other people’s systems and you will be learning how to do this and by learning how to
do this you are going to get better at creating what you want and so the second practice
life you may find out that you can create a lot faster because you’re much better at figuring
out specifically what you want and how to go about getting.

So those are the three big obstacles and resistances that I see come up for people when
figuring out what they want. The first one is that whole story of selfishness and how we
will have to look at how that word or words like that that we associate to getting what we
want, having what we want, going for what we want, we are going to have to reframe that
in terms of learning to be generous with ourselves and once we learn how to do that then
we can be generous with other people.

The second part is looking at the pain we associate with having what we want or it being
used to control our behavior so that we could get it where the disappointment of losing it.
How do we create the emotional reaction to that relationship? How does our desire in our
yearning get tied to pain? So you may want to inventory previous experiences with that
and break out the difference between going for what you want and having it and enjoy
there and what you did in the stories in your mind, the beliefs you made to create
unhappiness when it was lost or fell apart or what have you, the disappointment of not
achieving it and when you see that the process of going for what you want and having is a



                                                                                                               5/9

very different separate dynamic from craving the suffering about not having it then you
are like wow I can go for what I want and if I get it or I don’t get it I don’t ever have to do
this part because I can see all the signals and keep myself from playing those characters or
believe in the stories of those characters if that ever happens because that’s what created
the pain, the disappointment, the heartbreak, not the having and not the enjoying what
we’ve desired.

The third obstacle is don’t get overwhelmed by creating it for your whole life. Don’t try
and figure out that problem, just create a practice life, do a manageable step. So just focus
on the step in front of you and define what that step is and that step may be what you
want for this month and maybe what you want for this year or the next two years. And
then writing that plan that you are periodically going to reevaluate what you want and
refine it, make it better, so you don’t have to worry about getting it right.

So I am going to tell you a little bit about the process of defining and writing down what
you do want and you can break out that process into many different areas of your life,
personal relationship, professional relationship, family, money, career vacation into this
process for any of that but let’s take career for example. One way to look at it is what do I
want to have and that’s a 21:01 way to look at it but what about if we look at it in a
different way and say what do I want to be doing, what actions do I want to be taking, how
do I want to be expressing myself.

Instead of creating an image of success and saying that’s what I want to be, how about we
look at what are the expressions I make in the moment. What are the interactions that I
enjoy. Go back to your different careers or jobs and look at all the things you enjoyed
about them and what were the very specific things that you enjoyed. You may have had a
job that you really hated but there was something within that job that you really enjoyed
or one experience in that job that just made your day. What was it in that experience,
what were you doing, what was the environment of what you were doing that facilitated
that experience and that will help you figure out what you want.

That may not be the job but there were certain action or expression you were making in
that job that day that said this is fun I like doing this. If a job were like this I would be
doing this all the time. For me when I went back and looked at my job which was as an
engineering officer in the Navy one of the aspects I defined was I like solving engineering
problems, I like looking at the whole mechanical system, all the relationships between
hydraulics and electrical and mechanicals and pumps and valves and figuring out a
problem. If water is not getting from A to B or there’s a leak at point C how do you fix this
problem, that’s fun for me that engages this whole side of my engineering mind that I can
go analyze and problem solve.

What I didn’t like about doing it in the Navy was I was doing it very often with four hours
sleep or less. I own all the pumps and valves and if it didn’t work I was up all night
working on it to get it fixed. I was getting my guys up and they were working without sleep
to get it fixed. This was not fun then I figured out I want a job where I can solve
engineering problems but they are problems that I own, they are somebody else’s




                                                                                                               6/9

problems and I can come in and consult and help them solve their problems. I don’t have
to worry and stress about where the progress is so that’s what I mean about cutting down
to the details of what is it about an interaction about a job that you want.

When I was working for a Fortune 500 company we had a management development
program and as I’m going through this process of reevaluating my life I’m realizing that
managing people is not what I wanted to do and part of it was within that structure of a
large business at the time. The resources and the way that I wanted to manage and serve
people was not supported because what I realized, the way I really wanted to express
myself was I wanted to be in service to people, that’s how I viewed management but
management in this company viewed management as more of the authoritative, this is
you give them the guidelines, you give them the goals then you go make sure they
accomplish it and so is a very different style so I started look at sales I was like what does
the salesperson do and we think of used car salesmen but I was like really what does a
salesperson do is they help get the customer what they need.

So as a manager I looked at the employees as clients, I was like what do they need to get
their job done and I was like okay I want to give all these people this training and this
education and giving these resources and send them to classes and management looked at
me and said no that’s not going to happen, it’s not in the budget but when I looked at
being in sales and I say this is what I want to do for the client it had a complete different
spin I was like here I was serving a client who could support us and there would be return
on that effort then people were more willing to say you know what that’s a good idea and
so I realized that what I want to do was be in service then I had to redefine my role based
on how I wanted to express myself.

As it was I left the company but the next jobs I got were in sales. From the management
side I had permission to go the extra mile in trying to solve the client’s problem and I
didn’t have to be looking over my shoulder because management wasn’t concerned that I
was spending extra time and effort on a client so I changed the environment, I changed
the job based on what I wanted to express, not where I wanted to be, but what I wanted to
express and this is the kind of thing that you realize when you go back and figuring out
what you want is to go back to all those really enjoyable interaction and say you had at
work and say what is at the core elements of those interactions that I really enjoyed?

When I figured out these things that I wanted to be in sales and I wanted to be solving
engineering problems I got a job doing outside consultative sales for a company that did
pumps and valves and as much as I was doing sales calls and delivering people
equipment, defining the right pumps and valves and equipments that would help them do
their job I was also able to go in on sites where they had a problem and that we don’t
know what’s going on and I got to go in, troubleshoot different problems with valves and
steam systems and pumps and go play problem solver on somebody else’s ticket.

So in this way my management supported me going the extra mile doing service solving
problems for customers. That was part of how we built our relationships. It was fun. I got
paid to do things I enjoyed. So these are all the kind of little aspects to go back to your
other job and say what was really enjoyable about it, what wasn’t and that will help you



                                                                                                               7/9

define what you want by looking at the details of other past jobs and you can take the
same kind of analysis going back in inventory past relationships to define what you want
in relationships or what you don’t want or what you want in a partner or what you don’t
want.

So your mission if you choose to accept it in creating a new life you have to first figure out
and envision where you want that to be and the first step is figure out where you don’t
want it to be then you might see some obstacles. If you have trouble bringing to your mind
the ideas of what you do want to create, start looking perhaps the role of selfishness, fear
and pain of loss that you associate with having or getting what you want or feeling
overwhelmed because you have to get it right because you have to get it right, because you
have to define it for your whole life then implement some of the workarounds or
reinterpretations I provide about that or come up with one of your own.

Then to help figure out what you do really want, go back to previous experiences, the case
of a job, career, go back and define what it is you wanted to be like, do you want it to be a
really creative process, do you want to be working in teams with people, do you want to be
working alone, do you want to be serving people, do you want to be in charge of people
and by the way yes you can do both if the umbrella environment provides for it. The
umbrella environment doesn’t provide for it, maybe you need to find a different position
within that company. So going back and inventory things from your past and looking at
things not in terms of where do I want to be, what I want to accomplish but more in terms
of what expressions do I want to make and for me that meant problem-solving and I
didn’t know what the format was I just knew engineering problem-solving, was kind of
engaging and fun for me.

Service to people, helping people, watching them grow, although I didn’t do much in the
sales because that sales job was just one of my practice lives and as you define this list of
what are the aspects of the job, what are the aspects of a relationship that I want, aspects
of finances I want, it won’t look like a job, it’ll look like characteristics of a job,
characteristics of your personality and once you define what you want as far as how you
want to express yourself in these intangible ways then look and see what jobs fit that
profile of what you enjoy doing instead of trying to look at a job and say do I fit. No, first
define what you enjoy doing, how you enjoy expressing yourself, what environment you
want to be in then look at careers and say is that a good fit, look at businesses you want to
create and say is that a good fit. Look at how you are setting up your business and say is
that how I want to be living my life?

Once those pieces start to lineup and you’ve got an idea of where you want to go in your
relationships, in your career and your finances and what have you. So far as what you
want to create in your life the next step is to take action, actually sit down and write down
what can you do today, this week, this month and this year that are the steps you need to
make to go create that other life. We’ll talk later about what to do with that list once you
create it and how you are going to motivate yourself to go accomplish what’s on that list.





                                                                                                               8/9

Understand all this is much like a very iterative process it changes. It changes because you
change. What you want next year may not be what you want right now and that’s okay but
for right now pick a direction, go for something, practice creating it and when you do
figure out you know what, this is what I really want. You will have practiced some of these
steps that we are going to cover in this course so when you figure out what you do want all
of this comes much easier you will be practiced at it.

So a lot to do, some things to go back in inventory that comes up, some practice lives to
dream up in inventory specific ways you like to express yourself and interact. That will
become the list of what you want and specific action steps and all of this may take a couple
of weeks, may take a couple of months but this is the kind of process that you can do
ongoing or you can revisit every year as you re-create your life.

Probably the most important feature to consider when you’re creating your life is what
you want the emotional quality to be. What you want to feel when you’re at work,
recreating, you are in your relationships, you are at home, what do you want it to feel like,
what’s the emotional quality of your interactions with your clients, with your boss, with
your coworkers. What’s the emotional quality of the interaction, the humor, the fun, the
laughter with your partner, your mate, your friends and creating what you want, make
sure you notice the emotions and give them a place of proper do for you in defining what
you want in your next practice life.

I think that’s enough for now this has been Gary with a coaching session on creating what
you want in your life from pathway to happiness.com. Have fun out there.

Help Asking For What You Want

   pathwaytohappiness.com/blog/help-asking-for-what-you-want

                                                                                    March 8, 2016

Asking for what you want might seem like a simple thing, but it isn’t. It is a complex
process of noticing your desires, eliminating the selfish and unreasonable, feeling worthy
of having, feeling safe that you won’t be judged or rejected, finding the time and space to
be heard in our busy lives and competition for attention, and then phasing our request in
a way that they hear and feel how important it is to us. If you are at work all this might get
pushed aside because your priority is to take care of your boss’s needs, clients needs, and
co-workers so that you can keep your job and take care of your financial needs. If you are
a parent taking care of kids you might be so busy that you don’t have time to notice your
own needs. When there is a break in the action and you have time to slow down, maybe all
you notice is that you are too tired to want anything else. That is your sign that you need
time to rest by the way.

This isn’t the complete list of how to become aware of what you want and how to ask for
it, but it should help.

Know that wanting something for yourself isn’t selfish.

When you believe that asking for something that you want is selfish, you don’t allow
yourself to even ask. Often, when sub-consciously you feel it would be selfish, you might
even repress the desire for it, or quickly dismiss it mentally when the desire comes up.
This kind of self-negation can stop your request from getting out of your mouth, or distort
the way you ask so it is no longer clear that it is important to you.

Asking for what you want doesn’t mean you are needy.

Having desires, wants, and needs is a natural part of the human experience. We have a
desire for water when we are thirsty, and food when we are hungry. These aren’t the only
wants, needs, and desires we have as normal human beings. Other wants and needs that
are natural are for emotional connection, support, time for our self, freedom, empathy,
compassion, affection, understanding, sex, creativity, physical exercise, and to express our
own authentic voice. When we don’t have these needs met we get restless, frustrated, or
possibly depressed. Having wants and desires is natural. It doesn’t mean we are weak or
petty. It means we are human. Meeting our wants and needs is what helps us feel
satisfied and fulfilled.

Recognize that it is not the other person’s responsibility to provide what we
ask for.

It is their choice. They can say no, or negotiate for something in between. If you demand
or try to obligate another person to meet your needs and wants you may be interfering
with their freedom of choice. People we ask have their own needs and when we obligate
others we are not respecting what they need and want. If you ask someone and they say



                                                                                                               1/2

no, that has to be okay. If you become angry, annoyed, frustrated, or withdraw, then that
kind of emotional punishment is a sign that you are not respecting their choices. It is okay
if they say no. You don’t have to have all your needs and wants met by one person.

Tell the person you are asking how you feel and what it means to have what
you are asking for.

If you are asking for some time alone your partner might think you don’t like him and
reject himself with the lack of information. If you inform him that your time alone is how
you nurture your soul and spirit so you can be more of yourself and better with him, then
he is more likely to say yes, and feel good about it.

Always express appreciation.

If someone provides something you asked for then make sure they know you appreciate it.
A big hug with your words makes more of an impact. Getting appreciation from people,
particularly our partner is one way we get emotionally nourished in relationships. When
people are recognized and appreciated for what they do they feel better about doing it and
want to do it more. That means you will both be getting more of what you want.

Be reasonable and negotiate.

You might want that 2 week vacation to the Greek Islands this summer and you might not
feel it is selfish. That’s good. But your partner might not want to empty the bank account
to give it to you. That doesn’t mean he doesn’t love you. It just might be interfering with
his need to provide for the family long term. Listen to what your partner’s needs are and
how they can be met. Asking questions and listening to what your partner’s needs helps
them get their needs met. Sometimes they might not be able to articulate exactly what
their needs are. Those needs might seem like random thoughts and uncomfortable
feelings at first. Asking questions and providing a space to listen will help them identify
and articulate what they want and need. When you can help them get what they need in
the negotiation then they are more likely to give you what you want as well. You might
also discover that what you really wanted was a romantic dream getaway to a beach
island. You might find that the middle ground that gets both your real needs and wants
met is an island in the Florida Keys for a few days.

We let go of our desire – then you have to get it back

If we don’t try, then we don’t fail. If we don’t fail, then we don’t judge ourselves If we don’t
judge ourselves we won't’ feel bad. So the unconscious solution to “not feeling bad” is to
let go of desire so we don’t even try. But if you are dissolving the Judge, then it is safe to
have desires for what you want again.
